clue.text: Groups allowed into Tours

indicators.note: the word into tells us one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: tours are trips
allowed means let

explanation.surface: Parties are permitted to visit the French city of Tours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tours' looks like the French city, but it is just trips.
explanation.definitionFit: Sets of three people or things born or grouped together form such groups.

clue.text: On the way to Glastonbury, like Prometheus?

definitions.meaning: heading for a rock music festival, the Glastonbury Festival in Somerset
Prometheus was chained to a rock as punishment by Zeus

explanation.walkthrough: Glastonbury is a huge English music festival, so travellers are bound for rock; Prometheus was literally bound to a rock.
explanation.definitionFit: The word splits as music-festival travel and as being chained to a crag, the Titan's punishment.

clue.text: Where to find a flat, upper-class, first-rate-and a wealthy wife?

definitions.text: Where to find a flat, upper-class, first-rate-and a wealthy wife?

parts.note: a pad is a flat or apartment
A, as in A1, means first-rate

explanation.surface: A question about where one might find good lodgings and a rich bride.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Taming of the Shrew Petruchio comes to this Italian city to 'wive it wealthily', so the whole clue points there.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Petruchio seeks a rich bride in this northern Italian city, home to Katherina.

clue.text: Attention paid to tangled mass on head, which was important to Gwendolen and Cecily

definitions.text: which was important to Gwendolen and Cecily

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention
a nest is a tangled mass, as in a nest of wires
a ness is a headland or head

explanation.surface: Someone attends to a messy mop of hair, a matter that mattered to two Wilde heroines.
explanation.walkthrough: Gwendolen and Cecily in Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest each insist on marrying a man named Ernest, so being earnest is all-important to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Wilde's play title puns on sincerity, the quality the two young women prize in a suitor's name.

clue.text: Succumb after function's put off indefinitely

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
to succumb is to die

explanation.surface: A mathematical function is shelved for good once a person gives in.
explanation.walkthrough: SINE DIE is Latin for 'without a day', used of a meeting adjourned with no date fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Business adjourned with no date set for resumption is postponed without limit.

clue.text: People in G&S — they accompany airs

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: the letters G and S, as printed
a people is a race

explanation.surface: Characters in Gilbert and Sullivan operettas come along with the songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'airs' suggests songs in a Gilbert and Sullivan context, but the phrase is 'airs and graces'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'airs and graces' pairs affected manners with refined ones.

clue.text: What you might call Miss Grable from time to time?

indicators.note: taking letters only now and then signals every other letter of the name

explanation.surface: How one might address the film star Betty Grable now and again.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl or young woman, a Miss, is informally called this.

clue.text: Where Bertha Mason lived with a sailor? That's funny

parts.note: in Jane Eyre, Rochester's first wife Bertha Mason is kept in the attic
an old salt is a sailor

explanation.surface: The madwoman of Jane Eyre shares her quarters with a seaman, which seems odd.
explanation.walkthrough: Attic salt is refined, elegant wit, from the Athenians of Attica.
explanation.definitionFit: Refined Athenian wit is a humorous remark, a clever quip.

clue.text: Occasion on which to display books by Mrs Bunting

indicators.note: by means beside, so the pieces sit next to each other

parts.note: Eve Bunting is a children's author
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A festive occasion for showing off a writer's books, or bunting.
explanation.walkthrough: Eve Bunting is an Irish-American children's writer; the surface also hints at bunting hung at a fete.
explanation.definitionFit: A happening such as a show is an occasion for putting things on view.

clue.text: A Spanish hero that's keen

parts.note: El Cid is the Spanish national hero

explanation.surface: A sharp-witted Spanish champion.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words can mean sharp or cutting, as in a biting remark.

clue.text: Wild deer antler from which pots hang in some northern homes

definitions.text: from which pots hang in some northern homes

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters run free in a new order

explanation.surface: A stag's antler is used as a hook for cooking pots in northern cottages.
explanation.walkthrough: A randle-tree is a dialect word in Scotland and northern England for the bar across a chimney from which pots hang.
explanation.definitionFit: This dialect term names the beam or crossbar in a fireplace for hanging cooking vessels.

clue.text: A horse called Silver makes one highly emotional

parts.note: Silver Blaze is the racehorse in a Sherlock Holmes story

explanation.surface: Riding a horse named Silver makes someone excited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silver' suggests the Lone Ranger's horse, but the Conan Doyle story 'Silver Blaze' supplies the second name.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on fire is used figuratively of someone burning with passion.

clue.text: See someone about short order to offer a literary tribute

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the other

parts.note: to see someone romantically is to date them

indicators.note: short means a word cut by its last letter

parts.note: an edict is an order

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go out with a person after a curt instruction to honour a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Authors inscribe a book to a person as a mark of honour.

clue.text: Dug up hard deposit in calamitous disaster initially

indicators.note: in places the deposit inside the calamity word

parts.note: dire means calamitous
sinter is a hard mineral deposit from springs

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A disaster begins with something hard being excavated.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhumed or excavated things have been brought out of the ground.

clue.text: Meet us somehow protecting the King and Queen's soldiers

indicators.note: protecting means the scrambled letters wrap round the king
somehow says the letters come in some other order

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king
ER is the Queen, here with the 's

explanation.surface: Come and meet some royal guards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumas's heroes were armed guardsmen of the French king, carrying muskets.

clue.text: "- is as food, and needs no less Her Temperance over Appetite" (Paradise Lost)

definitions.text: "- is as food, and needs no less Her Temperance over Appetite" (Paradise Lost)

parts.words: "- is as food, and needs no less Her Temperance over Appetite" (Paradise Lost)
parts.note: a line from Book VII of Milton's epic, where Raphael warns Adam about curiosity: supply the missing word

explanation.definitionFit: Milton compares learning to food that must be taken in moderation, the theme of the forbidden tree.

clue.text: Master and Commander sounds like a slow burner

indicators.note: sounds like tells us the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: an Aga is a British range cooker that burns slowly and continuously

explanation.surface: A naval novel title is compared to a slow-starting success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master and Commander' looks like the Patrick O'Brian novel, but it defines an Ottoman title.
explanation.definitionFit: An Ottoman title for a military commander or master of a household.

clue.text: Philosopher to conceal, we hear, urge to sin endlessly

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is spoken

parts.note: to conceal is to hide
to egg on is to urge

indicators.note: endlessly drops the last letter

parts.note: to err is to sin

explanation.surface: A thinker hides, it seems, a temptation to do wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Martin Heidegger was a German philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Being and Time was a leading German thinker.

clue.text: One with honour to be William of Baskerville's sidekick?

parts.note: A is one
the DSO, Distinguished Service Order, is a British military honour

explanation.surface: A decorated man is to become a famous detective's assistant.
explanation.walkthrough: In Eco's The Name of the Rose the monk William of Baskerville is aided by the novice Adso of Melk; Baskerville wants to be Holmes.
explanation.definitionFit: Eco's narrator, a young novice, assists the Franciscan friar as Watson helps Holmes.

clue.text: Film director and Rosalinde's husband

definitions.meaning: Gabriel von ... is married to Rosalinde in Strauss's Die Fledermaus

explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet filmmaker and the operetta character share a surname.

clue.text: Curly et al with a bit of slapstick to go about on stage right and stage left

indicators.note: a bit of takes the first letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about turns the word round

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: right takes the right-hand end of the word, its last letter
left takes the left-hand end of the word, its first letter

explanation.surface: Comic actors with some slapstick move around the stage from side to side.
explanation.walkthrough: Curly, Moe and Larry were the Three Stooges, American slapstick comedians.
explanation.definitionFit: Curly Howard was one of the Three Stooges, comic foils.

clue.text: A satellite — it's eccentric, encircled by two rings

indicators.note: encircled by places one piece inside another

parts.note: a ring on the phone is a call
O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: eccentric means the letters are out of their usual order

explanation.surface: An orbiting moon moves off-centre within a pair of rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' and 'rings' suggest orbits, but 'two rings' is CALL and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Callisto is one of the large moons of Jupiter.

clue.text: A measure of what Holmes's game often was

parts.note: a foot is a measure of length

explanation.surface: A gauge of how a detective's quarry usually stood.
explanation.walkthrough: Holmes's catchphrase is 'The game is afoot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Holmes declares the chase under way with this word, meaning in progress.

clue.text: Kinglake's account of the East and nothing beyond that

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for East
O is nothing
then means beyond that, next

explanation.surface: A Victorian travel writer describes the Orient and what follows.
explanation.walkthrough: A.W. Kinglake's 1844 travel book about the Near East has a Greek title meaning 'from the East'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinglake's travel narrative of his journey through the Levant bears this Greek title.

clue.text: Burns hero, 49, an Asian

parts.note: Tam o' Shanter is the hero of a Robert Burns poem
IL is 49 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A character from Burns is described as a person from Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a people of southern India and Sri Lanka is an Asian.

clue.text: One intending to rob Fort Knox, or to pilfer

definitions.text: One intending to rob Fort Knox

parts.note: or is heraldic gold
to finger is slang for to steal

explanation.surface: A thief plans to raid the US gold depository, or to steal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' looks like a link word but is the heraldic term for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bond villain plans to raid the American bullion depository in the film.

clue.text: US lawyer with one on a mountain

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places one piece above the other

parts.note: I is one
a DA is a district attorney

explanation.surface: An American attorney takes someone up a peak.
explanation.walkthrough: Mount Ida is in Crete (and also Turkey).
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Ida in Crete is a peak of Greek myth.

clue.text: Note about silver: it's not one of their gifts

definitions.text: it's not one of their gifts

indicators.note: about places the first piece round the other

parts.note: mi is a note in sol-fa
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A remark about silver: it was not among the presents.
explanation.walkthrough: The wise men brought gold, frankincense and myrrh, not silver.
explanation.definitionFit: The three wise men gave gold, frankincense and myrrh, never silver.

clue.text: One accepted encompassing Parthenon's central section?

definitions.text: One accepted encompassing Parthenon's central section?

indicators.note: encompassing means the first pieces surround the next

parts.note: A is one

indicators.note: a central section means letters taken from inside the word

explanation.surface: A goddess is honoured by having a temple built around her.
explanation.walkthrough: The Parthenon housed the great statue of this goddess at its heart.
explanation.definitionFit: The Parthenon in Athens was the temple of the Greek goddess of wisdom.

clue.text: Producers of tack get music venue founder to include overture to Daphnis at start of season

indicators.note: to include means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Richard Sadler founded Sadler's Wells, a London theatre

indicators.note: overture to takes the first letter
start of takes the first letter

explanation.surface: Horse-gear makers commission a theatre founder to stage a ballet at the season opening.
explanation.walkthrough: Tack is horse gear; Sadler's Wells is a London dance and opera venue; Daphnis et Chloé is a Ravel ballet.
explanation.definitionFit: Makers of horse gear such as saddles and bridles are tack makers.
